mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their previous 12-month average signals deteriorating demand, which compresses corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12M avg and HOUST < 12M avg simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall below their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in INDPRO above its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals improving supply conditions, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO is above its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 2.0% coincident with a rise in CPIAUCSL above 3.0% YoY indicates a shift from restrictive to accommodative policy amid inflationary pressure, which initially boosts risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in PAYEMS above its 6-month moving average for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 6M moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 6-month moving average for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 and RSAFS above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals strengthening aggregate demand, which supports higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12M avg and RSAFS > 12M avg for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals persistent supply chain weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12M moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
